1125.body:
## 1. Problem description

When an Artifact version is materialized into a session workspace, the platform records a provenance
revision carrying the attribution: `origin: "system"`, `contentHash`, `artifactVersionIds: [version]`,
`publicationSequence`, `originMeta.kind: "artifact-materialization"`.

That revision is registered with a **wall-clock** `modifiedAt` (`new Date()`), while the file on disk
keeps its real mtime — and when the bytes already exist, the copy step returns early without touching
the file at all. The next workspace listing compares the recorded `modifiedAt` against `stat` and finds
them unequal, so it decides the file changed and appends a **new** revision built by
`reconcileWorkspaceFiles` that carries none of those fields (`origin: "unknown"`, no `contentHash`, no
`publicationSequence`, `artifactVersionIds: []`) — then points `currentRevisionId` at it.

Net effect: a listing refresh reduces the recorded attribution of an unchanged file. The delivered file
is still there and still correct; what is lost is the record of *who produced it and which Artifact
version it is*.

## 2. Minimal reproduction

No data mutation is required to see the mechanism; steps 4-5 are read-only.

    1. In a session, register an Artifact version V whose content bytes already exist at the target
       workspace path (e.g. promote a subagent deliverable that was copied earlier, or re-materialize
       the same version).
    2. Call materializeArtifact / the materialize path so that `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts`
       runs `copyCasToWorkspace({ reuseIdentical: true, ... })` and then
       `recordWorkspaceFileRevision(...)`.
    3. Read the revision row: it has origin="system", a contentHash, artifactVersionIds=[V] and a
       publicationSequence. Its modifiedAt is the clock value taken after the call.
    4. Call anything that lists workspace files — `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/artifacts` reaches
       `readWorkspaceFiles` in `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:106`, which calls
       `store.reconcileWorkspaceFiles(...)` at `:109`. (A run also does this when it emits
       `run.completed`.)
    5. Read the same file's `currentRevisionId` again.

Expected trigger condition: **whenever `reuseIdentical` returns early, or whenever the clock is read
after the write**, the recorded `modifiedAt` cannot equal the file's real mtime, so step 4 always
observes a change.

## 3. Expected vs actual

Expected — either of:
  - the revision that carries the delivery attribution remains the current revision, because a listing
    refresh is not a content change; or
  - if a new revision is appended, it inherits `origin` / `contentHash` / `artifactVersionIds` /
    `publicationSequence` from the revision it supersedes.

Actual — a second revision is appended with only `path`, `size`, `modifiedAt` (from `stat`),
`origin: "unknown"` and `artifactVersionIds: []`, and `record.currentRevisionId` is moved to it.
Consumers that read the current revision — the file listing, `getFileProvenance`, and any audit of
"which run/tool call/artifact version produced this delivered file" — now see an unattributed record.
A listing refresh permanently reduces the recorded attribution of an unchanged file.

## 4. Source location

All line numbers are from `main` = `18fa8353c2e0`.

    a. `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:31-32` — the clock stamp is what breaks the invariant:
           mode: "write", origin: "system", artifactVersionId: version.id,
           contentHash: copied.sha256, size: copied.bytes, modifiedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
       `:34` attaches `originMeta: { kind: "artifact-materialization", ... }`.

    b. `packages/cas/src/workspace-copy.ts:88` — makes the mismatch unconditional for identical bytes:
           if (input.reuseIdentical && existing.size === bytes) { ... return { transferId, bytes, sha256 }; }
       The function returns before the rename/link, so the file's mtime is never refreshed, while
       (a) has just recorded a `modifiedAt` taken after the call.

    c. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:106` and `:109` — the trigger: every file listing runs
       `store.reconcileWorkspaceFiles(...)`. Note `:137-138` in the same file registers with
       `metadata.mtime.toISOString()`, i.e. the correct pattern already exists here.

    d. `services/api/src/store.ts:5167-5168` — the condition that therefore always fires:
           } else if (reconciliationBaseline.get(file.path) === revision.id
             && (revision.modifiedAt !== file.modifiedAt || revision.size !== file.size)) {

    e. `services/api/src/store.ts:5169-5180` — the replacement revision: `artifactVersionIds: []`
       (`:5170`), `origin: "unknown"` (`:5175`), `modifiedAt: file.modifiedAt` (`:5174`), and no
       `contentHash`, no `publicationSequence`, no `runId`/`toolCallId`/`subagentId`/`originMeta`.
       `services/api/src/store.ts:5184` — `record.currentRevisionId = revision.id;` demotes the
       attributed revision to non-current.

    f. Same defect class at `services/api/src/remote-runner.ts:61` —
       `mode: "write", origin: "system", modifiedAt: new Date().toISOString(), size: file.size, contentHash: file.sha256`.

    g. Design-level gap in the vocabulary: `packages/schema/src/session.ts:263-271` enumerates
       `WorkspaceFileOrigin` as agent / mcp-download / remote-compute / subagent / system / tool /
       unknown / upload — there is no promotion or materialization value, and
       `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:376-380` falls back to `"unknown"` for anything it cannot
       classify.

Positive controls inside the same repository (so this is not a global overwrite):

    - `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:386` records `modifiedAt: fileStat.mtime.toISOString()`;
      `services/api/src/subagents/index.ts:174`, `:189` and `:224` likewise use `stat.mtime`. Records
      written through those paths are not demoted.
    - Files written directly by tools keep `origin: "tool"` and a `contentHash` across the same listing
      refreshes (see 5).

## 5. Runtime evidence

Read-only export of all 265 `workspace_file_revisions` rows of the audited instance
(volume `jd-fresh-test_data`, session `2ad3939c…`, run `c48cf34a-810d-4089-b8ca-ae467aa785af`,
executed version pinned by LF-normalized content hash to JD `30178fda77`; `materialize.ts`, `workspace-copy.ts`,
`artifacts/index.ts` and `remote-runner.ts` carry the same blob in SD `807982f0` and, as re-checked this
round, the same lines in live `18fa8353c2e0`).

Verbatim rows for one delivered file (265 revisions exported read-only from `workspace_file_revisions`):

    origin="system"   createdAt=00:41:29.590Z modifiedAt=00:41:29.557Z size=100724
                      contentHash="d0035d0d…" publicationSequence=296 artifactVersionIds=1
                      originMeta.kind="artifact-materialization"
    origin="unknown"  createdAt=00:41:29.603Z modifiedAt=00:41:29.532Z size=100724
                      contentHash=ABSENT publicationSequence=ABSENT artifactVersionIds=0   <== CURRENT

13 ms separate the two registrations. The unknown row's `modifiedAt` (00:41:29.532Z) is the file's real
mtime and is **25 ms earlier** than the `modifiedAt` recorded on the attributed row (00:41:29.557Z),
which is exactly the `new Date()` value from §4a — the discrepancy is arithmetic, not a coincidence.

Population and controls:

    - all 6 delivered files in that run show the chain `['system','unknown']`; current = `unknown`,
      `contentHash` absent, `publicationSequence` absent, `artifactVersionIds` 1 -> 0.
    - control files written by tools (`refs/doi_index.json`, `output/evidence_table.csv`) end their chain
      with `origin="tool"` and `hasHash=true` after the same number of listing refreshes.
    - the attribution existed right up to the promotion: the subagent-private workspace still carried
      6 revisions with `origin="subagent"`, `runId=subagentId`, `toolName="run_shell"`, per-call
      `toolCallId` and `contentHash`, the last at `publicationSequence=886`; the private file record was
      deleted at `01:10:41.794Z` and the promoted copy registered at `01:10:45.339Z`.

What this evidence does NOT prove: it does not show the file content, the Artifact version or the
download path being wrong — the bytes and the artifact record are intact (`contentHash` verified,
registration and read-back both fine). Only the workspace revision's attribution fields are lost.
It also does not measure how often a deployment lists files after promotion; it shows one occurrence
per delivered file in one run, on the delivered population 6/6.

## 6. Impact

    - Every consumer of the current workspace revision: the file listing, `getFileProvenance`, the
      provenance/audit views, and any answer to "which subagent run and which Artifact version produced
      this delivered file".
    - Promotion of Artifact versions into the session workspace (`materializeArtifact`) and remote
      compute deliveries (`remote-runner.ts:61`) — both clock-stamped sites.
    - Deliverables of multi-agent research runs are the visible class: the platform's own attribution for
      a peer-reviewed report degrades to `unknown` while the report itself is untouched, which inverts
      the trust signal for the most-reviewed object in the session.
    - Not affected: files written by tools, by the subagent handoff copy path, or by the recorder path
      (§4 positive controls).
    - JD note (informational, same defect class): the third clock-stamped site in our downstream build is
      `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:510` (workspace transfer commit). Whatever fix
      lands upstream we mirror it; we list it only so the site count is not under-stated.

## 7. Suggested fix direction

Ordered by invasiveness; we have not changed any code.

    (a) In `store.ts:5169-5180`, when the reconcile branch appends a revision, inherit
        `origin`, `contentHash`, `publicationSequence`, `artifactVersionIds` and `originMeta` from the
        revision being superseded. Smallest change, covers every clock-stamped site at once, and cannot
        invent attribution because it only carries forward what was already recorded.

    (b) Prefer a content test over a wall-clock test in `store.ts:5167-5168`: the attributed revision
        already carries `contentHash`, so a listing could treat `size`/digest equality as "no change" and
        skip appending entirely.

    (c) At the write sites (`materialize.ts:32`, `remote-runner.ts:61`), record `stat.mtime` instead of
        `new Date()`, matching `recorder.ts:386` and `subagents/index.ts:174/189/224`. Fixes the instance
        but leaves any future clock-stamped site exposed.

    (d) Add a promotion/materialization value to `WorkspaceFileOrigin`
        (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:263-271`) and stop mapping deliverable classes to `"unknown"` in
        `recorder.ts:376-380`, so the vocabulary can express what these files are.

(a) or (b) is what the observed data argues for: the loss happens in reconcile, not in the write.

## 8. Version note

    - Executed version of the audited instance: pinned by content hash (LF-normalized) to JD `30178fda77`;
      45/45 audited files match that ref, 40 of them also matching SD `807982f0`.
    - Attribution basis: `artifacts/materialize.ts`, `cas/workspace-copy.ts`, `artifacts/index.ts`,
      `remote-runner.ts`, `provenance/recorder.ts` and `runner/readiness.ts` are byte-identical between the
      executed build and SD; `store.ts` differs as a file but the defect lines
      (`:5167-5168`, `:5169-5180`, `:5184` at live main) are present on both sides, and the downstream diff
      hunks lie elsewhere (`:2291`, `:7264+`, `:7307+`, `:7757+`). Hence SD-side framework defect.
    - Re-checked against live `main` = `18fa8353c2e0` on 2026-11-12: all quoted lines still present, and no
      commit on those paths since fixes this (`materialize.ts` and `workspace-copy.ts` last touched by
      `77c6ef3d6` 2026-09-25).

1128.author: yuanzhou75
1128.body:
## What was observed

In a merge-queue `UT` run, a run that delegated to a `task` sub-agent **never reached a terminal state**: the parent run stayed `running` for the whole harness budget, and the worker then hung in teardown until the 600 s timeout.

This surfaced while landing #1119 (usage accounting for #1109), whose new test drove one delegated child. The test drove a real JiuwenSwarm adapter (`swarm:required` variant); the same file's non-swarm variant passed in 5.6 s.

### Evidence

Run `43170129650` (`event=merge_group`, `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-1118-…`), job `131022268344` (`UT`); artifact `ut-results` (id `13922896805`), `tagged/group-551`.

`worker-1-events.jsonl`:

```json
{"type":"test:fail","name":"a delegated child writes exactly one delegation-track usage row [science:…]","message":"expected run 50ce3a66-3068-417f-9e4c-4c4af8dcdf33 to become completed\n+ actual - expected\n\n+ 'running'\n- 'completed'\n"}
```

`worker-1-timing.json`:

```json
{"startedAt":"2026-11-12T06:50:40.652Z","durationMs":600018,"status":1,"signal":null,"error":"WORKER_TIMEOUT: 600000ms"}
```

`summary.json` for that group: `planned 11 / executed 11 / passed 10 / failed 1 / providerFaults 0`. The other ten cases in the **same** `[swarm:required]` group passed, including the **non-nested** `a multi-turn run's usage row is the sum of its turns`.

The same failure key appeared in a second merge-group run — `43171259633` (`pr-934`), job `131027783419` — because that group also contained the change.

## Why it matters

If this is the product path rather than the harness, a user who delegates to a sub-agent under this backend would see the parent run **stay `running` indefinitely**: no terminal state, no stream end, and — as far as this evidence goes — no turn budget cutting it. `providerFaults: 0`, so a provider error is not the explanation.

## What is *not* known

I cannot yet say whether this is a product defect (nested delegation under JiuwenSwarm never terminates) or a **test-harness** interaction (the stub gateway not being reached for the child). The swarm variant needs `bash` plus a ~1.5 GB swarm instance, which the development host does not have, so there is **no local reproduction**; everything above comes from the CI artifact.

Deliberately not claiming either conclusion here.

## What would settle it

1. In a live deployment, delegate one `task` child under the real JiuwenSwarm adapter and record whether the parent run reaches `completed` / `failed` / `cancelled` / `interrupted`.
2. **If it terminates** — the harness path is at fault (child not served by the stub gateway). Recorded here so the `swarm:required` tag can be put back on the delegated-child test.
3. **If it does not terminate** — nested delegation in the adapter hangs, and the parent's turn/step budget does not cut it. That is a product defect and needs its own fix.

## Current status of the test

To unblock the merge queue, the test was moved off the `swarm:required` variant (assertions unchanged: exactly one `delegation-track` row, parent `17/2`, child `7/1`, `invocationCount: 2`) and now runs on the built-in loop, plus a `finally` that cancels still-running runs so teardown cannot hang again.

**That means CI no longer exercises nested delegation under the real adapter** — which is exactly why this needs its own issue rather than being closed with the PR.

Related: #1109, #1119.
1128.title: [Bug]: a delegated child run never reaches a terminal state under the real JiuwenSwarm adapter

1132.title: [Bug]: Only the first proxied model call of an Evolve run reaches the usage ledger; every later call is silently deduplicated

1133.author: JinhZhao
1133.body:
## 1. Summary

On the JiuwenSwarm executor, the link between a model call and the provider response it belongs to is stored in a single mutable field on the recorder (`responseId`). It is **written synchronously** by the event path and **read later, from a queued task**, by the code that writes the `model.completed` record. Neither call passes the identity as an argument, so the value a record gets is whatever the field happens to hold when the queue drains.

Across four completed runs, **54 of 303 `model.completed` records carry no `responseId` even though a response with the same `evidence.turn` did emit one**. The correlation existed and was lost on the way to disk.

## 2. Expected behaviour

A model completion record should carry the identity of the response it completes, bound **per call**, and that binding should not depend on scheduling:

- `assistant.response.started` arrives with `responseId` (`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts:940-944`);
- the `model.completed` record for that same call (`versioning.ts:259`) should reference that id.

The recorder already takes the identity as a parameter for other work — `recordObservation({ …, sequence })`, `afterTurn({ turn, … })` — so a per-call binding is the established shape here; `responseId` is the exception.

## 3. Actual behaviour

`responseId` is process state on a shared object. It has one setter, two clearers, and one consumer that reads it on a different tick from the setter.

## 4. Source code

All paths relative to the repository root, quoted at main `f0efd382e`.

### 4.1 One mutable field, one setter, two clearing points

```ts
// services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts   (AgentVersionRecorder — the single recorder for both executors)
:155  private currentTurn = 0;
:156  private responseId?: string;                     // the only place the correlation lives
:185  async beforeTurn({ turn, history } …) {
:187    this.currentTurn = turn;
:189    this.responseId = undefined;                   // clearing point 1 — runs inside the recording queue
:213  async afterAssembly({ turn, assembly } …) {
:214    // The new response ID is allocated by the loop after assembly, including retries.
:215    this.responseId = undefined;                   // clearing point 2 — also inside the queue
:245  event(event: RunEvent<U>): AgentEventEvidence {
:246    if (event.type === "turn_start") this.currentTurn = event.turn;
:247    if (event.type === "response_start") this.responseId = event.responseId;   // the ONLY setter — synchronous
:251    return this.evidence();
:254  async modelCompleted(result: unknown): Promise<void> {
:259    await this.record("model.completed", undefined, undefined, this.evidence(), this.modelAction);
:285  private evidence(): AgentEventEvidence {
:287    … turn: this.currentTurn,
:288    ...(this.responseId ? { responseId: this.responseId } : {}) };   // snapshot at read time, not at call time
```

### 4.2 The write is synchronous; the read is queued

```ts
// services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts
:286  private emit(event: AgentEvent): void {
:288    const evidence = this.trajectory?.evidence(event as { type: string; responseId?: unknown; turn?: unknown });
:290    for (const listener of this.listeners) listener(tagged);      // no queue on this path
:940  case "assistant.response.started": {
:943    this.emit({ type: "response_start", responseId: String(event.responseId), turn });

// services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts
:82   private turn = -1;
:171  modelRequest(input) { return this.run("model_request", async () => { … this.turn += 1;
:177      … this.recorder!.beforeTurn({ turn: this.turn, history }) … }); }      // clears, on the queue
:192  modelCompleted(turn, history) { return this.run("model_completed", async () => {
:195      await this.stage("model_completed", () => this.recorder!.modelCompleted(turn)); }); }  // reads, on the queue
:208  evidence(event) { …
:216    const runEvent = event.type === "response_start"
:217      ? { type: "response_start", responseId: String(event.responseId), turn: this.turn }
:219    return this.recorder.event(runEvent as never);                 // sets, synchronously
```

### 4.3 The await on the queue is not the guarantee it looks like

```ts
// services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts
:501  if (!auxiliary) { last = undefined; lifecycle?.beforeTurn?.(); }   // turn_start per call
:523  await prepare();          // → observer.request → queued beforeTurn + afterAssembly (both clear)
:558  await record(turn);       // → observer.completed → queued modelCompleted (reads)
:351  const observed = auxiliary ? undefined : observer;   // housekeeping/compaction calls are never observed

// services/api/src/agent-run/recording-wait.ts
:6    /** Stop waiting, not the underlying write. Keep handlers attached for late failures. */
:7    export function waitForRecording<T>(work: Promise<T>, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
:9      const abort = () => reject(signal.reason ?? new Error("Recording wait cancelled"));
```

`waitForRecording` returns control to the caller on abort **while the queued write keeps running**. So the ordering that §4.2 appears to provide (`prepare` drains, then the response starts, then `record` drains) is only guaranteed for calls that are not aborted — and an aborted call is exactly the case where a later turn's `beforeTurn`/`afterAssembly` can clear the field before the earlier `model_completed` reads it.

### 4.4 Who consumes the field (this is user-visible, not just audit)

```ts
// packages/trajectory/src/server.ts
:117  if (contextRef && typeof event.responseId === "string") responses.set(`${agentId}:${event.responseId}`, `context:${contextRef.digest}`);
:281  const contextId = contextRef ? … : legacy?.contextId ?? call?.contextId ?? responses.get(`${item.agentId}:${String(event.responseId ?? evidence.responseId)}`);
:285  if (contextId && typeof (event.responseId ?? evidence.responseId) === "string") responses.set(…);

// apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx
:295  function findAssistantByResponseId(entries, responseId) …
:300  function findThinkingByResponseId(entries, responseId) …
:377  if (last?.type === "thinking" && last.turn === event.turn && last.responseId === undefined) {   // adopt an unstamped placeholder
:482  … && entry.responseId === undefined && entry.turn === event.turn) adoptIndex = index;
:497  if (entry.type === "thinking" && entry.responseId === event.responseId && entry.status === "running") …
```

A missing id pushes the trajectory server onto the `legacy?.contextId ?? call?.contextId` fallback (`server.ts:281`) and pushes the timeline onto turn-based matching, where an unstamped placeholder can be adopted by whichever response arrives (`RunTimeline.tsx:377`, `:482`). A wrong id attaches one response's thinking block to another response.

## 5. Reproduction

Observed on four existing completed runs (read-only pass over their run records; no agent was re-run).

| Run | `model.completed` rows | with `responseId` | without | `assistant.response.started` records | **without id, but a started record exists at that turn** | without id and no started record at that turn | started ids never appearing on any completed row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `c48cf34a…` | 108 | 93 | 15 | 111 | **14** | 1 (turn 54) | 18 |
| `483d89ca…` | 33 | 30 | 3 | 31 | **1** | 2 (turns 1, 2) | 1 |
| `71987d15…` | 104 | 76 | 28 | 101 | **25** | 3 (turns 1, 3, 5) | 25 |
| `324a1e1f…` | 58 | 39 | 19 | 57 | **14** | 5 (turns 1, 3, 6, 7, 14) | 18 |
| **Total** | **303** | **238** | **65** | **300** | **54** | **11** | **62** |

Ordering evidence from one run (`483d89ca…`), the earliest missing-id row and its neighbours:

```
2026-11-12T02:17:48.813Z  model.completed              turn=1   responseId=<absent>
2026-11-12T02:18:22.525Z  model.completed              turn=2   responseId=<absent>
2026-11-12T02:18:24.269Z  assistant.response.started   turn=3   responseId=356e99dd-e7b5
2026-11-12T02:18:26.093Z  model.completed              turn=3   responseId=356e99dd-e7b5
```

Turns 1 and 2 recorded no identity while turn 3, handled by the same code a second later, recorded it — so this is not a capability gap in the executor; the field simply held nothing at read time.

**A deterministic unit reproduction does not need a live run**: construct an `AgentVersionRecorder`, call `event({ type: "response_start", responseId: "r1", turn: 1 })`, then `beforeTurn({ turn: 2 })` (or `afterAssembly`) and only then `modelCompleted(result)`. The resulting `model.completed` evidence carries `turn: 2` and **no** `responseId`, although the response it completes is `r1`. This pass did not execute that test, so it is stated as a design check rather than as a measured result.

## 6. Scientific impact

1. **A model turn cannot be tied back to the provider response that produced it** for 54 of 303 turns (17.8 %). When a claim in a report traces to a `model.completed` record, the record can name the turn but not the response, so re-deriving the exact prompt/response pair for that turn is not possible from the record itself.
2. **Silent, partial and non-reproducible.** No error is raised and nothing is logged. The rate of "id lost although a started record exists at that turn" per completion row differs by run — 13.0 % (`c48cf34a`), 3.0 % (`483d89ca`), 24.0 % (`71987d15`), 24.1 % (`324a1e1f`) — so an audit that spot-checks a few records will sometimes see nothing wrong.
3. **Downstream correlation is heuristic, not authoritative.** The trajectory server's response→context map (`server.ts:117`, `:285`) is only populated from stamped records; the web timeline adopts unstamped placeholders by turn proximity (`RunTimeline.tsx:377`, `:482`). Both degrade to guessing exactly for the rows where the identity is missing.
4. **62 started responses never reach a completion record.** Whether those calls ended without a completion or the identity was dropped is not distinguishable from the surviving data — which is itself the cost of the design: two different failures produce the same artifact.

## 7. Suggested fix direction

1. **Bind the identity per call instead of per recorder.** Allocate the response id alongside the turn in the object the queue already carries (the `pending` entry at `jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts:196`), and pass it into `modelCompleted` so the record is stamped from a parameter, not from `this`.
2. **If a field must stay, make the loss visible.** When `evidence()` is called for `model.completed` with `responseId` unset while a `response_start` for the same turn has been seen, that is a detectable inconsistency — log/count it instead of dropping it silently.
3. **Make the queue the only writer.** Both clearing points already run inside the queue (`:189`, `:215`) and the only setter does not (`emit` → `event` at `:247`). Routing the setter through the same queue would serialize the field; the correctness fix is (1), and (3) at least removes the cross-domain interleaving.
4. **State the contract in a test** next to `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`, which already drives `assistant.response.started` with `responseId: "r1"/"r2"` at `:225-231` and `:255-262`, but asserts only event order (`:239-245`, `:721`), never what lands on the completion record.

## 8. Relation to existing reports (why this is filed separately)

- **[#710] / PR #711** (closed, merged `84c81b80`) fixed the **desktop display layer** for response events — 4 files under `apps/desktop/`, no server-side change. Neither `native-agent/versioning.ts` nor `agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts` appears in it.
- **[#978]** mentions `assistant.response.started` only while enumerating events of a stuck run; no attribution claim.
- Searching all 469 current issues and their comments: `response_start` = **0 hits**, `currentTurn` = **0 hits**. Nothing on record describes this correlation.
- **#1125** and **#1128** are about Artifact provenance reconcile and delegated-child terminal state respectively — different subsystems.
- Open PRs touching candidate-adjacent files: #311 and #965 edit `agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` (`+4` and `+32/-8`), so line numbers in §4.2 may shift; **no open PR touches `versioning.ts` or `jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts`**, i.e. nothing in flight fixes this.
- No action on any of those issues is requested here.

## 9. Version this was measured against

- SD `main`: `f0efd382e5e79260386ce89674eef7af1bbc05a9` (2026-11-12T08:49:00Z).
- `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts` sha256 `7e9be52faf60a667e96692ef2030f14b704e129c2d8998c680e069007008896d`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts` sha256 `ae61b67aa5bfab0165743818d3606cec21b0992754c9cfb31a8d37ee6d6487d7`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/recording-wait.ts` sha256 `4b9530f167e3d2b9f88fafa42279a6c8e944d8a083499c60c2397b460556ec53`.
- Run records: existing data volume, read-only.

## 10. What this report does and does not establish

**Established (CONFIRMED):** the correlation is carried in one mutable field, written synchronously and read from the queue, with two queue-side clearing points and no per-call binding; and 54 of 303 completion records in four real runs lost an identity that had been issued.

**Not established (NEEDS MORE EVIDENCE):** the opposite failure mode — a completion stamped with a *neighbouring* call's id. It is structurally possible for the same reason the loss is, but it is **not observable in this data**, and one check that looks like it would catch it does not: "does a completion carry an id belonging to a different turn's started record?" returned **0 rows in all four runs**, because both records take their turn from the same counter (`jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts:216-218`), so a mis-bound id still agrees with its neighbour by turn. Separating "dropped" from "mis-bound" needs a run with timing instrumentation (e.g. logging the field value at set, clear and read for one turn), which was out of scope here.

**Inherited, not re-derived:** the 11 "no started record at that turn" rows were sub-classified in an earlier analysis as 2 genuinely unstarted plus 9 compaction-driven. This pass reproduced the 65 = 54 + 11 partition only; the 2/9 split was not recomputed and is not relied on above.

1135.author: yuanzhou75
1135.body:
## What happens

`scripts/start-stack.test.mjs::a leftover backup from a hard kill is restored on the next start` fails intermittently — twice on the same head, 13 minutes apart — with a **zero-length** read of the fixture file it is waiting on:

```
the recovery happens before the first sync, so uv never resolves against the mirror content
+ actual - expected
+ ''
- 'version = 1\n# committed resolution\n'
    at scripts/start-stack.test.mjs:145
```

Both occurrences: same test, same assertion, same head (`1ee9f6fb`), same job — run `43207232310` attempt 1 (job `131156525367`) and attempt 2. `planned 7631 / executed 7631 / passed 7630 / failed 1`, everything else green, `providerFaults: 0`.

Nothing in that head touches `scripts/`: the pull request behind it (#1134) changes `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts`, `remote-runner.ts`, `agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts`, `subagents/index.ts` and one test file. `scripts/start-stack.test.mjs` and `scripts/start-stack.mjs` have no commits since 2026-11-11, so main and the head run the same script.

## Most likely cause: the test polls for the fixture file's *existence*, not its content

```js
// scripts/start-stack.test.mjs:137-145
await writeFile(
  join(bin, "uv"),
  `#!/bin/sh\ncat uv.lock > "${seenFile}"\nexit 0\n`,
);
...
const run = launch(root, bin, []);
await waitFor(() => existsSync(seenFile), "the first sync to run");
assert.equal(await readFile(seenFile, "utf8"), PRISTINE, ...);
```

The shell performs the `>` redirection — creating/truncating `uv-seen-lock.txt` — **before** `cat` runs. `waitFor(existsSync)` can therefore return while the file is still zero bytes, and the assertion reads the empty file. On a loaded runner that window is wide enough to hit twice in a row; on an idle machine it almost never is. That makes the failure a property of the test's synchronisation, not of the code under test.

## The alternative I cannot fully rule out

`recoverLeftoverLockfile` (`scripts/start-stack.mjs:319-334`) restores the backup with `copyFileSync`, which truncates the target before writing it. It runs synchronously at startup, well before the fake `uv` is invoked by `uvSyncProject`, so a reader should never observe the truncated state — but if a future change makes that path asynchronous or moves it next to the sync, an empty `uv.lock` would produce exactly this message too. Worth stating so the fix does not assume the first cause without checking.

## Suggested fix (test-only)

Wait for content rather than existence, e.g. `waitFor(async () => (await readFile(seenFile, "utf8").catch(() => "")) === PRISTINE, "the first sync to read the restored lockfile")`, or have the fake `uv` write to a temporary name and `mv` it into place so the polled path only ever appears complete. The second occurrence also demonstrates that a plain re-run is not a fix: retrying the job reproduced it.

## Impact

Any pull request's `UT` can go red on this alone, and a re-run is not guaranteed to clear it (it did not here), so it costs a full ~13-minute CI cycle per attempt and hides real regressions in the same slice.

Not touched: no code change is proposed to `scripts/start-stack.mjs` here, and this issue does not belong in #1134's scope.

1140.author: JinhZhao
1140.body:
## 1. Problem description `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/research-package/preview?defaults=1` computes **five** export profiles (`necessary`, `complete`, `completeWithTrajectory`, `completeWithMemoryGraph`, `completeWithTrajectoryAndMemoryGraph`) in one request. Two of those five walk the session's content-addressed trajectory closure, and that walk reads and `JSON.parse`s every record object in the closure. On a real session in our test instance the closure is **7 740 objects / 3 202 534 318 bytes** (5 442 of them record objects, 3 186 108 662 bytes). The frozen integrity path over exactly that closure takes **56.0–57.2 s** per profile. The five profiles are submitted through `Promise.all` but serialized on a **single global promise queue**, so one dialog open costs at least `2 × 56 s ≈ 112 s` of serial work (derived, see §5.3). The web client does not wait that long: - `apps/web/src/research-package/export-preview-cache.ts:47-49` sets `setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10_000)` — **without an abort reason**; - `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx:152-159` catches the rejection and calls `errorText(reason)` (`:49`, `reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : …`), so Chromium's internal string — `signal is aborted without reason` — is rendered verbatim in the export dialog; - because `preview` stays `undefined`, `files` stays `[]`, and `:235` renders `researchPackage.noWorkspaceFiles` ("当前会话没有工作区文件。") for a session that actually has **176 workspace files**, while `:243` disables both export buttons (`disabled={… || !preview}`). So a user opening 导出证据包 on a long-running session sees: two rows stuck at 正在计算大小…, then a browser-internal exception string, then a claim that the session has no workspace files, and an unusable 立即导出 button. Nothing in the server log looks like a failure — the work finishes after the browser left (2 970 × HTTP 200 out of 2 999 `defaults=1` requests in our log dump), which is why this is invisible server-side. The existing `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` contract does not help here. It is raised when `canWarm` returns false, i.e. **when a run is active** (`services/api/src/research-export-previews.ts:103`, `:119`, `:173`, `:200`), and `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1450-1452` only turns it into `202` if the client sent `Prefer: respond-async` — which the web client does (`apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts:138`) and maps to a **localized** message (`:139-151`). Open a session with a long history (ours: 176 workspace files, 226 catalog file rows, 7 740-object closure). 2. 更多会话操作 → 导出证据包. 3. Within 10 s the dialog shows the raw `signal is aborted without reason`, `已选择 0/0 个工作区文件`, `当前会话没有工作区文件。`, and both export buttons stay disabled. ## 3. Expected vs actual | # | Actual today | Expected | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `AbortError` from the client's own 10 s timer is rendered verbatim (`signal is aborted without reason`) | The dialog recognises its own cancellation (`isAbortError`, which already exists at `apps/web/src/api/client.ts:86-88` and is used by chat paths) and shows localised "still preparing" copy instead of a browser-internal string | | 2 | A failed/absent preview renders as `当前会话没有工作区文件。` while the session has 176 files, and both export buttons are disabled | "unknown yet" and "empty" are different states; an empty list is only claimed when the server actually reported zero files | | 3 | A slow preview holds the HTTP request open for ~56–112 s | The pending contract is not only for a busy runtime: a preview the client cannot get inside its budget should answer `202`/`EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` (or a job handle) and let the client poll | | 4 | One `defaults=1` request computes five profiles, serialized on one global queue, and re-walks the whole trajectory closure once per trajectory profile | The two trajectory profiles should share one closure walk, and sizing should not require deserialising every record | | 5 | Server logs show 2 970 × 200 for this route | A `200` that arrives after the caller aborted is not evidence the user got a preview | ## 4. The client budget is 10 s ⇒ a factor of ~11; raising it to 60 s would still leave the request at ~0.5× of the required time, which is why "just increase the timeout" is not a fix. Note also that an aborted HTTP request does not cancel the server-side computation, so each retry adds queued work. **5.4 What is NOT the driver — RECORDED (negative results)** | candidate | result | | --- | --- | | workspace file count | 176 files scan = 8.77 / 10.04 / 15.81 ms (`Infinity` limit), 8.56–9.45 ms at the default limit; a raw readdir+stat replica = 7.19–8.40 ms; a 14 932-file tree = 640–684 ms. Five profiles × scan = 45–110 ms, i.e. **<0.1 %** of 112 s. Real defect, immaterial latency. | | `/app/node_modules` in the scan | correctly ignored (25 512 files on disk, 8 returned) | | memory-graph export | `duration_ms=0`, 1.9 MB store | | concurrency contention | interval-overlap count vs elapsedMs over 32 samples: Pearson **r = −0.465** → rejected | | session/closure scale vs the logged `workspace_snapshot` samples | ρ = 0.275, r ≈ −0.14…−0.03 → rejected, because those samples are censored: `recordingStage` logs `completed` only when `tracing \|\| slow \|\| aborted` with `slowAfterMs = 30_000`, so every logged sample is structurally ≥ 30 s and cannot measure a fast snapshot | | server errors on this path | none. The route answers 200/202. `/app/data/logs/api.log` (span 2026-11-11T23:44:17Z → 2026-11-12T13:21:56Z, 2 540 lines) holds 2 028 `http_request_failed` lines = 2 023 × `statusCode=401` and 6 × `statusCode=404`; **0** of them mention `research-package` or `preview`. | **5.5 Not measured (and why)** - **Queue wait with an active run**: creating a run writes into the audited instance, which was out of scope for this read-only audit. The mechanism is stated from code (§1, `assertCanCalculate` → `canWarm` → `409`), not from a measurement. - **End-to-end wall time of one `defaults=1` request**: the server log carries no duration field for this route, and measuring it live would enqueue real preview work on the audited instance. - **A full closure-size growth series**: single point plus two smaller real closures (§5.1). ## 6. Impact - 导出证据包 is unusable on long-trajectory sessions from the web client: the size estimate never arrives, and the buttons stay disabled. - The user is shown a browser-internal exception string and a false statement that the session has no workspace files — the two most misleading things this dialog can say. - Every dialog open (and the 3 s re-arm) enqueues five profiles on one global queue, which also delays other sessions' previews and background `tick()` warms. - Server-side observability is misleading: the route reports 200 for work that finished after the caller gave up. - This is the same cost mechanism behind #1085's heap exhaustion; #1085 removed the *trigger* (warming on a plain session read, commit `5fc09fc8`) but not the per-request cost, so it can still be reached from the dialog itself. ## 7. Suggested fix direction Ordered to match what the user actually sees; none of these is a timeout bump. 1. **P0 — treat the client's own cancellation as cancellation.** Use the existing `isAbortError(reason)` helper in `ResearchPackageActions.tsx`, and give the abort a reason (`controller.abort(new Error("preview-budget-expired"))`) so nothing can leak a browser string. 2. **P0 — never render "no workspace files" from an unknown.** Keep the empty-state only when the server returned `files: []` for a successful preview; render a distinct "scope not determined yet" state otherwise, and keep export reachable through the existing background/async path. 3. **P1 — make "slow" answer like "busy" does.** Reuse the `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` / `respond-async` contract (already implemented end-to-end) for a preview that will not finish inside a budget, instead of holding the request open; or make `defaults=1` return the requested profile only and let the other four be computed lazily when the user changes the switches. 4. **P1 — one closure walk per request, shared by the profiles that need it.** The two trajectory profiles currently walk the same 3.20 GB closure independently. 5. **P1 — drop the single global serial queue** (or make it per-session/per-project) so one session's five profiles do not serialise, and do not serialise behind other sessions. 6. **P1 — size without deserialising.** `addPreviewObject(..., bytes.byteLength, "log")` needs a length, not a parsed object: `stat`/`ref.size` gives it, and the dependency walk could read the record's dependency list only. At 968.7 MB/s vs 64.6 MB/s this turns ~56 s into a few seconds. 7. **P2 — scale-aware budget/cache policy** (e.g. derive the client budget from a cheap closure-size probe, or keep the previous revision's estimate visible while recomputing). 8. Related but separate: `complete` previews bypass the shared listing cache and re-run `reconcileWorkspaceFiles` five times per dialog open — five directory *writes* to produce one read-only estimate. The write-side consequence is filed separately as #1125; here it only matters as redundant work. ## 8. Version note - Anchors and all quoted code are on **SD live main `8a37206be19e4f4d92f52dfa0f08873383a1d50f`** (per-file git blob SHA and size recorded in §4). - Re-verified at submission time (2026-11-12T13:42Z) against **`2d9aa5d344b63b4dca55f92fc3077d0e55d2643d`**, which is one commit ahead of that baseline. The newer commit is the #1125 fix (`fix(api): record the delivered file's own mtime so a listing cannot demote it`) and touches `agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts`, `artifacts/materialize.ts`, `artifacts/materialize.test.ts`, `remote-runner.ts`, `subagents/index.ts`. All nine anchor files above are **byte-identical** between the two revisions (git blob SHA and size compared per file), so the defect is live on current main and every line number quoted here still applies. - **Merged PR #1035** (2026-11-10, `fix(research): prevent export preview OOM and finalize excluded-cache executions`) already rewrote parts of `research-export-previews.ts` (+65 −9) and `research-snapshots.ts` (+61 −26) to bound preview memory — streaming CAS validation, incremental trajectory measurement, memoized JSON byte counts, cancellation on scope deletion/shutdown. Its merge commit `1aeb6598ad05c2692b3ab58d04c16b44ad1f57a0` is an **ancestor** of the baseline used here (`compare` status `ahead`, 172 commits), so every number in §5 was measured **with #1035 already applied**. #1035 addressed the heap ceiling; the ~56 s per-profile duration, the per-object sizing reads at `research-snapshots.ts:597-598`, the one global serial queue and the 10 s reason-less client abort are all outside what it changed. - Open-duplicate check at submission time: 85 open issues (title-filtered on export / package / preview / trajectory / research / timeout / abort / performance / slow) plus the changed-file list of all 35 open PRs filtered against the nine anchor paths. The only open PR touching this area is #1136 (`Preserve Evolve candidate sources in research packages`, `research-snapshots.ts` +82 −5), which extends what an export contains — it does not change how expensive computing a preview is. - Measurements were taken on a Docker test instance built from our fork tip `30178fda7`, which is behind main by `5fc09fc8` (the #1085 fix). Everything cited above exists on main independently of that commit; the session-read warming is explicitly *not* claimed as a live main defect. - Relation to existing issues: - **#1085 / PR #1086 (closed)** — same cost mechanism, different trigger; that fix removed the plain-session-read warm and reduced the background warm to one profile. The per-request five-profile cost and the client-side error handling are untouched. - **#1079, #1083 (closed)** — `complete` + full trajectory failures reported as bare `404`s, with no root cause claimed in either report. This issue is about the *cost* path and the web client's 10 s budget, a different symptom (a held-open request, not a 404). - **#1099 / PR #1103 (closed)** — mapped a preview `ENOENT` race onto the pending contract; the remaining gap is that "slow" has no pending answer at all (§1). - **#1013 (closed)** — bounded the export/copy *task* polls; the *preview* abort path is separate. - **#1024 (open, feature)** — desktop-first export UI redesign (honest size, pending explanation, durable export center). It asks for the presentation half; this issue is the server-side cost and the web client's error handling, and is reproducible without any UI redesign. - What is *not* established here: no end-to-end `defaults=1` wall-clock measurement, no active-run queue-wait measurement (both would have written to the audited instance), and therefore no claim about the exact total a user waits — only that one profile's closure walk is 56 s and two of five profiles perform it behind one serial queue.
1140.title: [Bug]: Research-package preview needs ~1 minute per trajectory profile while the web dialog aborts at 10 s, surfacing a raw AbortError and a false "no workspace files"

1152.author: yuanzhou75
1152.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Session export/import (research package, `.sdresearch`) is capped today by **two independent limits**, and neither is visible anywhere in the UI:

1. **Uncompressed archive total: 512 MiB** — `packages/research-package/src/index.ts:15` (`MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024`). It bounds the *uncompressed* tar on both sides: export estimate and refusal at `:229-231`, import inflation at `:134` (`gunzipSync(..., { maxOutputLength })`), `:141`, `:155`.
2. **Compressed upload: 256 MiB** — `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1472` and `:1495` call `readBytes(request, 256 * 1024 * 1024, "Research package")` for `POST .../inspect` and `POST .../import`. `services/api/src/http/body.ts:29` raises `Research package exceeds the 268435456 byte limit` (`PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`), mapped to HTTP 413 at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:4604-4605`.

What a user sees today:

- **Export over the cap**: the background export fails *after* the whole scope has been read, with the raw English string `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`. The desktop dialog shows `task.error` verbatim (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx:169`), while the size preview (`预计大小（未压缩）`, `ResearchPackage.tsx:342-345`) never mentions a limit.
- **Import over the cap**: the upload is refused with a raw byte count, also in English (`ResearchPackage.tsx:269` → `role="alert"` at `:355`).

**The two caps are inconsistent, so an export the app allows can be impossible to import.** With incompressible content the archive stays close to its uncompressed size — measured below, a 300 MiB payload exports as a ~300 MiB `.sdresearch`, which is already over the 256 MiB import cap. "Export succeeds, import answers 413" is therefore reproducible by construction, with no unusual data.

**Measured cost of the current pipeline** (x64 Windows, Node 22, `--max-old-space-size=3072` to match the API default in `services/api/src/heap-budget.ts:23`; incompressible payload; values are `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` over one export followed by one import):

| payload | archive (compressed) | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| 256 MiB | 256.1 MiB | 1,071 MiB |
| 300 MiB | 300.1 MiB | 1,248 MiB |
| 500 MiB | 500.2 MiB | 2,056 MiB |

The marginal cost is consistently **~3× the payload** (payload + whole tar buffer + gzip output), so peak RSS ≈ 3 × payload + ~300 MiB. At the current 512 MiB cap that is already **~1.8 GiB**.

Nothing here is one buffer that could simply be raised: the exporter reads every object into memory (`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:605`, objects collected at `:340-349`), then builds the entire tar in one buffer and gzips it (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:120-125`), and the importer inflates the whole archive with `gunzipSync` and keeps views into that single buffer (`:132-160`).

Extrapolating the same slope: 1 GiB ≈ 3.3 GiB RSS, 2 GiB ≈ 6.3 GiB, **5 GiB ≈ 15.3 GiB**. A 5 GiB cap cannot work on a normal 8–16 GiB machine with this pipeline — it would OOM or thrash before the cap is reached. Raising the constant alone would turn a clean refusal into a crash.

## Design Ideas

Target: **5 GiB uncompressed by default, configurable** (for example `SCIENCE_AGENT_RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES`), with the import upload cap *derived* from it instead of being a second literal. Reaching 5 GiB requires the pipeline to stop materialising everything, so this is best staged.

**Stage 1 — make the limit visible, and honest (small change)**

- One shared source of truth for the cap, exported from `@sciencediscovery/research-package` and returned by the preview response as an additive field (next to the existing `estimatedBytes` / `estimateKind`, `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:700`).
- Render it in both dialogs next to the estimate (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`). When `estimatedBytes` exceeds it, refuse **before** any packaging work and say so, pointing at 必要导出 (`level=necessary`) as the way forward.
- Offer an explicit override that requires a second confirmation naming the risk in plain words (may take a long time, may exhaust memory), localized in zh-CN and en. This is the requested behaviour: over the cap → suggest the necessary export; otherwise warn and confirm twice.
- Derive the upload cap from the package cap (`readBytes(..., packageCap + overhead)`) so every package the exporter can produce is importable. Today's 512 MiB export vs 256 MiB import is a round-trip defect.
- Localize both over-limit errors; do not surface raw byte counts or internal English strings.

**Stage 2 — stream, then raise to 5 GiB**

- Export: stream tar → gzip → output file (`ResearchPackageExports` currently receives a fully built `Uint8Array`, `services/api/src/research-package-exports.ts:127-135`), and pass object *sources* (paths) rather than `Uint8Array` so objects are not all resident.
- Import: stream `gunzip` into a temp file, verify per-object checksums while copying into CAS, and stop buffering the whole archive (`http/index.ts:1472/1495` via `readBytes` needs a temp-file sink).
- Preflight free memory and free disk before starting, and refuse with a clear message instead of failing mid-way (the estimate already exists, so this can be checked up front).
- Then raise the default to 5 GiB (configurable).

**Stage 2 caveat — the per-file tar field.** `MAX_FILE_BYTES = 32 GiB` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:12`) cannot be represented by the current 12-byte octal size field (`writeOctal(header, 124, 12, size)` in `tarHeader`, ~8 GiB maximum). While the total cap stays ≤ 5 GiB this is unreachable, but if single objects are ever allowed to grow, switch to GNU base-256 encoding or cap the per-file value at 8 GiB.

## Involved Public APIs

- `GET /api/projects/:id/research-package/preview` — additive fields only (`maxBytes`, optionally the level it applies to). No existing field changes or removals.
- `POST .../research-package/inspect` and `POST .../research-package/import` — accept larger bodies once the cap is derived from the package cap. The 413 path remains, with localized text.
- Nothing renamed or removed. Desktop and Web both consume these endpoints, and both dialogs need the same copy.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `#1024` (export UI redesign) explicitly excludes the 512 MiB policy from its scope; this issue is exactly that excluded piece, and its UI work (limit line, over-limit confirmation) should land together rather than collide.
- `#1105` (explicit API heap budget) and `#1035` (export preview OOM) show memory pressure has already caused incidents; the measurement above is the same mechanism at the package boundary.
- The API heap budget defaults to 3072 MiB (`services/api/src/heap-budget.ts:23`). Buffers are off-heap, but RSS still competes with the runner and the JiuwenSwarm instance on the same machine.
- Desktop saves the archive through the native dialog, the Web client downloads through the browser (`apps/desktop/src/api/research-package.ts:52-55`); both need the over-limit path.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit** (`packages/research-package`): boundary at the cap (±1 byte), the refusal message, an incompressible payload; a package at exactly `maxBytes` exports and imports.
- **API** (`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`): the preview returns `maxBytes`; an over-cap preview/start is refused early with the localized message; an oversized upload yields 413 with localized text rather than the raw byte count; round-trip a package whose compressed size exceeds the old 256 MiB cap.
- **UI** (desktop tests): the limit is rendered; over-limit disables start and points at 必要导出; the override requires the second confirmation; zh-CN and en strings both covered.
- **Performance evidence** for the PR: export+import peak RSS at 256/300/500 MiB with the harness described below, before and after the change.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` for the static gate, `pnpm test:shared` for the full CI plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The cap is one shared value, returned by the preview API and rendered in both dialogs.
- [ ] An over-limit export is refused before packaging starts, with a localized message that suggests 必要导出.
- [ ] An explicit override exists and requires a second confirmation naming the risk; both languages covered.
- [ ] Import accepts every package the exporter can produce (upload cap derived from the package cap), proven by a round-trip test whose compressed size exceeds 256 MiB.
- [ ] Over-limit import/inspect errors are localized and do not print raw byte counts.
- [ ] After streaming: the default cap is 5 GiB (configurable) and a 5 GiB-class export/import completes on a 16 GiB machine without exhausting memory, with the measured peak RSS recorded in the PR.
- [ ] `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared` pass.

## Additional Information

Reproducing "allowed export, impossible import" — no unusual data required:

1. Put a ~300 MiB incompressible file in a session workspace (for example a `.bin`/`.zip` of random bytes; it becomes a package object).
2. Export it: the preview shows ~300 MiB (under the 512 MiB cap), the export completes, and the resulting `.sdresearch` is ~300 MiB — over the 256 MiB import cap.
3. Import that file: the upload is refused with `Research package exceeds the 268435456 byte limit`.

The measurement harness creates a package with one random `sha256`-addressed object and imports it, recording `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` after each step; it runs against `packages/research-package/dist/index.js` and needs no API server.

The user report that triggered this: the 512 MiB limit blocks exporting real sessions, and the requested behaviour is a substantially larger cap (5 GB suggested) plus "over the cap → suggest the necessary export, or warn and ask for a second confirmation".
